email.body1:
John, saw Bitsight crossed $200M ARR and topped the latest Forrester Wave for cyber risk ratings.

Momentum like that usually means more in-market accounts than the team can cover before pipeline catches up, and that is where deals go cold. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a signal play for Bitsight off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them tend to progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
John, quick follow-up for Bitsight.

Past $200M ARR, the bar on net-new pipeline keeps rising faster than headcount can, and most teams cannot say exactly how many meetings they need to hit the number. The gap shows up late and the quarter turns into a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Bitsight needs to close that gap, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
John, last bit of proof for Bitsight.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to the CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Bitsight's reply rate likely compares to other cyber and risk vendors. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. Running revenue at this scale is its own kind of busy and I get it.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to an enterprise cyber motion? I will tailor it to Bitsight either way.
